context: Interactive force-directed network graph (data visualization) showing a 60-node social network where node size encodes influence with a togglable scale (linear/sqrt/log) and color encodes sentiment via a diverging palette
first_impression: Polished and readable network with a deliberate Tol diverging palette, clear typographic hierarchy, and a genuinely thoughtful educational interaction — toggling scales with live explanatory annotations
what_works: The Tol diverging color palette (blue through neutral to red) is a deliberate non-default choice that encodes sentiment cleanly; the scale toggle with contextual annotation explaining perceptual distortion is an unusually thoughtful interaction that earns its place. Neighborhood highlight-on-hover with opacity dimming is well-executed.
what_doesnt: The force simulation settles nodes into a compact cluster that occupies roughly the lower 60% of the 1200×800 SVG, leaving a noticeable empty band across the top of the chart area — a layout inefficiency that makes the whitespace feel accidental rather than intentional. The size legend circles use flat gray fills, missing an opportunity to show the actual sentiment-color encoding on representative nodes.
